column1: # THE OPERAND WALK'S ADJUDICATION TABLE.  srcwalk_worklist.py joins every
# (isa, mnemonic, register) that LOSES a published source register when the
# Capstone operand walk is deleted -- the exec171 price, 540,798 encodings --
# to these rows, and REFUSES on any losing signature that matches none, on any
# that matches two, and on any row here that matches nothing.
# THE ONE QUESTION EVERY ROW ANSWERS: does the ENCODING NAME the register?
# REAL-OPERAND      the encoding names it as an ordinary operand and QEMU does
#                   not state that read.  Remedy: a statement at QEMU's
#                   decoder.  A wire change; owes R13.
# REAL-VOCAB-GAP    the encoding names it and QEMU reads it, but the tracer
#                   has no declared regfile row to name it WITH.  Remedy: a
# REAL-QEMU-ELIDES  QEMU's chosen lowering drops a register the encoding
#                   names.  R15 verbatim: that is NEVER grounds to remove it
# SUPERSET          the encoding does NOT name it, or a standing ruling says
#                   the read does not exist.  The walk over-named it and the
#                   wire is RIGHT to drop it.  Needs the ruling AND a
#                   whole-population arm -- plausibility is not a verdict.
# OPEN              no verdict.  MUST carry the question and the method that
#                   would answer it; the instrument refuses an OPEN row with
#                   no question mark in its note.
# only banked pair in which arm B is the walk-deleted tree.  Counts in the
# notes are reg-INSTANCES over that pair unless they say encodings.

column6: R7.3 ("REG_ZERO exists, so it should be specified... We should not be dropping reg zero") + R15 + R16; exec174/MIPS_ZERO_ARM.txt
column7: THE LARGEST CLASS IN THE PRICE AND IT IS NOT A SUPERSET. 128,774 instances. WHOLE-POPULATION FIELD ARM over every losing encoding: 128,754 carry a 0 in rs or rt, and the other 20 are MSA insert/fill/ctcmsa whose GPR operand sits in the ws field -- bin (rs!=0, rt!=0, rd==0) is exactly 20. So 128,774 of 128,774 NAME register number 0. THE EXTERNAL LEG IS ONE WITNESS, NOT THE POPULATION, and is written that way on purpose: llvm-mc -triple=mipsel renders 00000080 as `lb $zero, 0($zero)`. The whole-population llvm-mc arm is OWED -- it was started and had not finished when this row was written, and a citation to a measurement that has not returned is exactly the silent false success this tree refuses. The field arm is the proof; LLVM corroborates one row of it. The remedy is a QEMU-side statement, not a deletion.
37 instances on bfxil/extr/wfet. EVERY ONE of the 37 losing encodings disassembles with xzr or wzr in its operand text -- 37/37, not a sample. Same shape as the mipsel class and the same remedy.

column6: R15 (c.mv verbatim: "we express the zero register... QEMU making an optimization does not mean we accept it as architecturally correct"); zext.w is defined as add.uw rd, rs1, x0; FILED at exec159
column7: 8 instances, all c.zext.w (Zcb). NOTE THE INSTRUMENT LIMIT: llvm-mc prints the ALIAS and so its text cannot witness x0 -- the naming is in the ISA's DEFINITION of the alias, not in LLVM's output, and this row rests on that definition, not on a disassembly arm.

column6: champsim_tracer_qemu_regs_aarch64.h -- 181 lines, declares svcr (REG_VCTRL) and has NO ZA row; #332 second-row-source precedent; llvm-mc -mattr=+all renders 00008080 as "fmopa za0.s, p0/m, p0/m, z0.s, z0.s" and 0000e0e1 as "st1q {za0h.q[w12, 0]}, p0, [x0, x0, lsl #4]"
column7: 63,232 instances over 13 mnemonics, every one of which READS ZA: the six outer products accumulate into it, the ZA-slice stores take their store DATA from it, addha/addva accumulate. The encoding names it -- LLVM prints it as an operand -- and QEMU reads the array; the tracer simply has no declared row to name it WITH, so the walk is the only source of the word. A vocabulary gap, not an over-name. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THAT CORROBORATES IT: the ZA-slice LOADS (ld1*) WRITE ZA and do NOT appear in this losing set at all.

column6: R7.1 at include/exec/insn-dataflow.h -- "the fact that a register's upper contents may not be modified does not imply it is a source"; llvm-mc renders 030008c0 as "zero {za0.d, za1.d}"
column7: 9 instances, and they are the one mnemonic in the REG_MATRIX set that does NOT read ZA. `zero` writes the selected tiles and leaves the unselected ones UNCHANGED, which is exactly the R7.1 preservation shape a source list may not encode. Carved out of a64-matrix-za deliberately: writing the whole register class REAL would have justified nine rows with a reason that is false for them.

6,122 instances, ALL sysl. QUESTION: sysl's operand is the system register the op0/op1/CRn/CRm/op2 fields select -- the encoding plainly names it, so why is this not already a statement?

9,749 instances, top mttr/mtc0/mtc2/mftr. QUESTION: the MT/CP0 movers' GPR operand -- named by rt?
7,984 instances, top mftr and the MSA compare family. QUESTION: fcr31 carries the FP condition codes and the rounding mode -- architectural source under R16?

6,900 instances, the DSP multiply-accumulate family (dpax.w.ph, dpaq_sa.l.w, maq_*). QUESTION: an accumulate reads its accumulator, which is the #228 GENUINE-ACCUMULATE shape -- does that reading carry, and is ac0..3 named by the encoding's ac field?
2,368 instances: mftr 1,288, mfc0 768, sdbbp, tlt. QUESTION: REG_SYSMMU on mfc0 is one of the three 96-B must-0 rows -- does this bucket resolve with that item or apart from it?

1,152 instances: mfc2 768, mftr 384. QUESTION: CP2 is implementation-defined -- is there an architectural register to name, or is this the one bucket where the walk names something the ISA leaves undefined?

799 instances, top addwc/rddsp/pick.qb/pick.ph -- DSPControl. QUESTION: pick.* reads the DSPControl condition bits, rddsp reads the register itself; addwc reads the carry. Real on their face, but which register does the wire mean by REG_FLAGS here?
424 instances, top mftr/mthc1/movn.s/movn.d. QUESTION: does the FR=0 pair rule reach this bucket?
209 instances, top addqh.ph/mul.ph/addqh.w/subuh.qb at 9 each. QUESTION: a DSP arithmetic op with an ABI-named register operand -- which field names it?

column6: target/riscv/insn_trans/trans_rvv.c.inc, the note_vector_config_read() comment: "NOT ON vsetvl/vsetvli/vsetivli... those instructions WRITE vtype and vl and compute the new values from their operands (vsetivli from two immediates, reading neither register)"; do_vsetivli() at :248 passes two TCG constants and writes only rd; R7.1
column7: 96 instances and the losing mnemonic set is EXACTLY {vsetivli} -- no vsetvl, no vsetvli, which is the line the source comment draws. The one vset form that DOES read vl (vsetvl with rd==0 and rs1==0, "keep the current vl") reads cpu_vl through a real op the walk already sees, and it does not appear in the losing set. Capstone's REG_VCTRL source is an over-name; the wire is RIGHT to drop it.

column6: target/riscv/insn_trans/trans_rvv.c.inc, ldst_whole_trans()'s comment: "THE LOAD FORMS GET NOTHING, and the asymmetry is the point. For vl4re8.v the other three registers are DESTINATIONS. Capstone publishes them in the source list because its operand model marks the whole group; R7.1 says a destination is not a source, so the drop on that half is RIGHT and stating it here would fabricate three reads"
column7: 88 instances over 12 mnemonics and EVERY ONE IS A LOAD FORM -- vl2r/vl4r/vl8r and their e16/e32/e64 spellings. Zero store forms (vs*r.v) appear in the losing set, which is the asymmetry the source comment predicts: the STORE half's group members are stated by QEMU as real reads, so they never lost anything. The mnemonic pattern is scoped to the load forms on purpose -- a store form appearing here later must REFUSE as unclaimed, not be absorbed by a rule written for its opposite.
